dedupe_keys.name: newts integrated dataset national energy water treatment and speciation and its dashboards

description: The NEWTS Integrated Dataset version 1.0 is a unified, standardised database of energy-related wastewater chemistry in the United States, with more than 400,000 sample records from 27 state and federal bodies and scientific publications, many with locations. The EDX page says it covers produced water and other oil and gas wastewaters, mine drainage, coal ash leachate and power plant wastewater, and was built to support treatment decisions and to identify potential critical mineral sources. A State-Level Database Dashboard shows a subset, and the NEWTS Economic Data Dashboard for critical materials for energy screens the concentration and potential value of 18 critical materials in produced water, brackish groundwater, acid mine drainage, coal combustion residual leachate, flue gas desulfurisation wastewater and geothermal fluids. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC-BY (version not stated; NETL EDX lists 'Creative Commons Attribution'). Coverage is national. Caveats: source data differ in methods and detection limits, and the economic dashboard is a screening tool, not a resource estimate. For simulation it gives located wastewater volumes and chemistry for treatment plant, water reuse and mineral recovery scenarios at mines and power plants. Related catalogue records include the NETL National Critical Minerals Data Dashboard and the EA discharges from abandoned metal mines data. Access is through the provider page linked in this record.
